title: VM-first launcher, retained Docker mode, and bounded recursion
objective: Make the provisioned VM the eventual default one-command Little Mester workflow while preserving host-Docker as ./lab-docker, keeping setup separate from fast daily launch, and enabling explicitly opted-in, depth-bounded recursive self-testing. Follow-on child work for parent epic #35; do not switch the ./lab default until #35's VM adoption gates pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: After all parent #35 VM adoption gates pass, ./lab <workspace> launches or reuses the outer VM and enters the direct guest OpenCode TUI by default; setup/provisioning is not repeated on normal starts, and explicit diagnostics/satellite commands remain available.

The existing host-Docker single-agent workflow remains usable as ./lab-docker, without Docker-in-Docker, host Docker socket exposure, or implicit recursive-agent capability; ./lab is not switched before VM release gates pass.

README documents fresh setup, normal startup, end-of-day behavior, and exact effects of up/status/ssh/agent/stop/down/base/rebuild, including which commands preserve or delete VM overlay, guest workloads/volumes, auth data, and control keys. A safe non-destructive stop/resume lifecycle is available before recommending daily VM use.
Default VM workspace sharing excludes the Little Mester repository unless an explicit recursion option requests it; host path validation and sensitive-path refusals remain enforced.

--recurse and --unsafe-recurse are explicit, distinct modes; unsafe-recurse enables self-modification and implies the required repository view, while recurse alone does not silently authorize self-writes.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local Bats cases cover unsafe-recurse implying recurse and requiring a workspace containing the checkout, plus safe workspace snapshots are copied into a separate checkout. Full VM/host behavior remains unverified.

acceptance_criteria.text: A maximum nesting depth is configurable by an explicit flag, defaults to 0, is propagated/enforced across every child launcher, cannot be reset or increased implicitly, and refuses over-depth launches before starting a VM/agent.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local Bats cases cover default depth 0, explicit max propagation, nested increment, missing opt-in, reset/increase rejection, CLI max parsing, profile metadata, and refusal before prerequisite checks. No live nested VM acceptance claimed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A disposable outer-agent self-development loop can modify a selected checkout, start a separate nested Little Mester instance to test those changes, retain/clean nested state explicitly, and continue the outer session; nested execution does not expose additional host paths, host Docker, credentials, LAN, or broader egress.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Local tests cover persistent isolated snapshots, dirty/untracked content, excluded .mester/.little-mester.conf, escaping-symlink refusal, separate profile roots, and explicit cleanup protections. Nested KVM/session/isolation acceptance remains pending.

needed: Measure clean setup/provisioning separately from warm daily startup; verify warm startup avoids package/image rebuild and enters the TUI with one command.

Exercise fresh install, up/reuse, interactive launch, normal shutdown/resume, and destructive down/rebuild on disposable VMs; assert retained/deleted overlay, guest volumes, auth, logs, and keys match docs.
Run host-Docker workflow as ./lab-docker and verify it remains a single agent with no host Docker socket and no nested agent/VM capability.
Test default workspace does not include repo; test --recurse inclusion and --unsafe-recurse write authority with all path guards.
Test max-depth defaults to zero; test boundary depths, propagation, attempts to reset/increase depth, and fail-closed behavior before child startup.
On a supported KVM host, run the full self-development loop using a disposable workspace/nested VM and verify outer session remains usable and host isolation/egress invariants hold.
Test on unsupported nested-virtualization host and verify clear refusal without weakening outer boundary.

On an owner KVM host, launch with workspace A, exit the TUI, then run the one-command launcher with workspace B. Confirm the prompt and verify /workspace maps only B, QEMU/virtiofsd reuse the existing profile and qcow2 overlay, installed OpenCode is not reinstalled, and workspace A/B host data is unchanged except for deliberate test markers. Also rerun with B to verify same-workspace warm launch does not reboot. Stop if guest shutdown fails or current workspace cannot be verified; do not use --clean, stop, or down.

Before committing launcher changes, run the CI Bats suite (`bats tests/vm.bats`) and ShellCheck gate (`shellcheck --severity=error lab-vm lib/vm/lifecycle.sh`) in an environment where installed; current guest lacks both. These do not replace live VM acceptance.

After the code is committed/shared and when the current #41/#45 host handoff permits another action, test workspace A/B/same-workspace warm reuse on a disposable named profile (`./lab-vm run <A> --name launcher-smoke`, then B, then B again). Preserve the existing default profile and host-Docker session; do not use --clean, stop, or down. Verify /workspace mapping, retained overlay, no guest harness reinstall, and unchanged host workspaces. Follow #41's current handoff and stop conditions first.

ORDERED FOLLOW-UP: first complete #41's current egress-reload/models-status gate, then owner-verify same-profile warm switching (workspace A → B → B, retaining the overlay and avoiding reprovisioning). Only after that passes, implement bounded recursive/nested self-testing under #43/#52 before default migration: max depth defaults to 0, is propagated and cannot be reset, refusal occurs before child startup, child workspace/state and network boundary are independently enforced, and unsupported nested KVM fails clearly. Keep host-Docker mode and do not merge/default-switch based on local mocks alone.

On owner KVM host, test the outer workspace A/B/B warm-switch gate first per current #41 handoff; then test a supported nested KVM profile and verify depth propagation, max-boundary refusal before child startup, separate guest workspace/state, independent restrict=on/proxy/host-LAN boundary, parent-session continuity, and recursion-clean behavior.
On an unsupported nested-virtualization guest, verify the /dev/kvm preflight refuses before workspace copy, VM provision, or agent startup; preserve the outer VM and existing host-Docker session.

Exercise --recurse with the Little Mester checkout and verify host checkout remains unchanged while the snapshot is writable; separately verify --unsafe-recurse requires a workspace containing the checkout and grants only the explicitly selected workspace.

SUPERSEDES the earlier ORDERED FOLLOW-UP wording that placed implementation after the live A/B/B host check: bounded-recursion implementation is being developed on feat/bounded-vm-recursion as explicitly requested; live nested KVM/isolation validation remains blocked until the current #41 host handoff permits it, and default migration remains gated.

For safe top-level repository snapshots, verify recursion-clean initial-<profile> refuses while the associated outer VM profile is running, then removes the snapshot only after the outer VM is stopped; verify normal nested-profile cleanup also refuses live QEMU/virtiofsd/proxy processes.

CORRECTION to the prior note that Bats/ShellCheck are unavailable in the guest: that was based only on `command -v` in the OpenCode execution runner, not an inspection of the VM. Investigation found guest cloud-init omitted both packages although CI installs them separately. Fresh VM provisioning now adds Bats and ShellCheck; generated cloud-init and local regression/schema checks pass. The existing owner VM has not been modified or queried, so availability there remains unverified until the #41 handoff permits a guest check.

CORRECTION to the immediately preceding cloud-init note: Bats/ShellCheck are not part of base guest provisioning. They are optional on-demand packages installed into an already-running selected profile by `./lab-vm install-tools [--name <profile>]`; `--restart-opencode` relaunches the direct-guest TUI after installation, and `-v`/`-d` propagate diagnostics. User must exit the current TUI first. The script does not boot/reprovision/restart the VM, and the current owner guest was not modified. Mocked SSH/profile tests and the complete 50-test VM Python suite pass; live use awaits the #41 gate.

2026-11-01 implementation in feat/bounded-vm-recursion: added explicit --recurse, --unsafe-recurse, and --max-depth (0-32; default 0); nested VM launches require opt-in, increment inherited depth, reject max-depth increases/resets and refuse over-depth before prerequisites/startup. Direct guest agent launch persists and exports current/max depth. Local tests are in progress; no nested KVM, VM boot, TUI, or host-isolation acceptance claimed.

2026-11-01 workspace isolation: safe repo-related outer workspace uses a private persistent snapshot; nested profiles copy the selected workspace into ~/.cache/lab-vm-recursion/<profile>/workspace and use a separate VM state root. The snapshot helper creates independent Git metadata, preserves dirty/untracked files, excludes .mester/.little-mester.conf, refuses escaping symlinks/special files, and reuses without overwriting. recursion-clean requires explicit confirmation/--yes and refuses a live profile. Local tests are in progress; no live child lifecycle acceptance claimed.

2026-11-01 parser discovery: the existing path-shorthand check treated the repository agent/ directory as a workspace when invoked as lab-vm agent; command recognition now takes precedence over path shorthand. The execution environment carries LAB_VM_RECURSION_DEPTH=1 without a maximum (legacy marker), which correctly fails closed for nested startup until launched by the new profile metadata path.

2026-11-01 local validation after teardown guard: Bats 142/142, Python 66/66, documentation consistency 115/115, ShellCheck, Bash/Python syntax/compile, and git diff --check passed. No nested-KVM/host acceptance claimed.

2026-11-01 teardown hardening: down, stop, rebuild, and up --clean refuse recursive-state loss before side effects; explicit --discard-recursive warns and permits teardown. Possible descendant state remains recorded after a lowered maximum and is cleared when the associated overlay is deleted.
